page.title: Virtual Event Production Guide for Buyers
page.description: Learn the key decisions, platforms, staffing, and timelines you need before launching a virtual or hybrid event. Covers platform choice, production crew, backup streams, and cost models.
page.h1: What should you decide first about virtual event production?
page.definition: Virtual event production is the end‑to‑end process of selecting a streaming platform, designing a run of show, rehearsing speakers, staffing a live crew, and delivering a backup stream so the event runs without a single point of failure and recording for on‑demand distribution.
page.quick_answer: Choose the platform and lock the production crew before you finalize the agenda; then schedule a full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before go‑live.

sections.h2: Which streaming platform fits my event size and budget?

blocks.p: Start by matching attendee capacity and budget to one of the three cost models: per‑host licences, self‑serve monthly plans, or annual enterprise contracts. The platform is not the production; someone still has to own the run of show, rehearse speakers and keep a backup stream ready.

ul: Per‑host licence platforms such as Zoom Webinars
Self‑serve monthly studios such as StreamYard and Livestorm
Enterprise suites sold on annual contracts such as ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, Goldcast

sections.h2: What production roles do I need for a webinar versus a summit?

blocks.p: A simple webinar can be run by one producer, while a summit or hybrid event requires a show caller, speaker manager, moderator, and platform operator. Staffing scales with complexity.

sections.h2: How far in advance should I plan a hybrid conference?

blocks.p: Lock the venue AV and the streaming platform six to eight weeks before the event, then finalize the agenda. Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final.

ol: Schedule full rehearsal two to five days before
Run technical check 60 minutes before go‑live

sections.h2: What backup and accessibility measures are required?

blocks.p: Provide a redundant stream, closed captions, and a downloadable recording within 24 to 48 hours. Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours, while attendees still remember the event.

ul: Edited recording and short clips delivered within 24 to 48 hours

sections.h2: What are the typical cost ranges for produced events?

blocks.p: Moderated webinars typically cost $2,500 to $7,500 per production, while executive summits and hybrid conferences start at $10,000 and can exceed $50,000. Platform and production are two purchases: the platform is software; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream.

faq.q: How do I choose between a self‑serve studio and an enterprise suite?
faq.a: Match the expected attendee count and internal technical skill to the cost model; self‑serve studios suit up to a few hundred viewers with minimal setup, while enterprise suites provide dedicated support, advanced analytics, and scalability for thousands.

faq.q: What is the minimum crew for a live hybrid event?
faq.a: At least four people: a show caller to cue transitions, a speaker manager to coordinate presenters, a moderator for audience interaction, and a platform operator to monitor streams and backup feeds.

faq.q: When should I schedule the full rehearsal?
faq.a: Run a complete rehearsal on the actual platform two to five days before the live date, then perform a final technical check sixty minutes before going live to verify audio, video, and backup paths.

faq.q: What accessibility features are mandatory for public events?
faq.a: Provide real‑time closed captions, an optional sign‑language interpreter, and ensure the recording includes captions and audio description; deliver the accessible recording within twenty‑four to forty‑eight hours.
